minutes.headline: Select Board heard the state delegation, set six state funding priorities including primary school AC, and objected to the APDC's handling of the 30 School Street demolition filing.
minutes.summary: The board met with the legislative delegation about FY23 state budget priorities, heard an ARPA outreach presentation, and received the town manager's five-year financial forecast. It voted to approve a revised list of legislative funding priorities, reinstated an auto dealer license, appointed four cultural council members and approved a manager license amendment. Members sharply criticised the Architectural Preservation District Commission over delays on the 30 School Street certificate to alter.

public_comment.topic: School Committee chair objected to the capital planning committee's priority for primary school air conditioning and asked about ARPA funds.

Capital planning committee member, speaking as a citizen, defended the charter capital planning process and said the AC proposal lacked an electrical upgrade and might be better served by split systems.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to approve a revised list of state legislative funding priorities, adding primary school air conditioning and dropping 925 Mass Ave.
Members criticised the Architectural Preservation District Commission over delays on the 30 School Street certificate to alter, and said they will review its bylaws and procedures.
The board heard the state delegation on the FY23 state budget, including a Chapter 70 increase in the governor's budget.
The town manager presented a five-year financial forecast that shows a small FY23 surplus and deficits in later years, since it does not assume free cash.
The board voted to reinstate a Class II auto dealer license, appointed cultural council members as a group, and approved an amended manager license for Extopa Cantina.

why_it_matters: The priorities list is the town's request to the state delegation for budget help, and primary school cooling is now on it, which touches the School Committee's capital plan and ARPA spending.
The forecast shows deficits after FY23 because it assumes no free cash, so later budgets and any tax levy or override question depend on whether free cash is available.
watch_next: The board's review of the Architectural Preservation District Commission's bylaws and procedures, and a possible town meeting article setting deadlines for it.
Board brainstorming on the ARPA presentation, and the postponed select board liaison appointments at a later meeting.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the four votes and on most dollar figures, including ARPA, the free cash and staffing-plan amounts, the capital requests and the library fee. Several items appear in only one record. The tractor purchase amount is the one clear conflict, and two votes are worded differently enough to check.
